title: The Fourier transform of the density is the partial Fourier transform of the kernel
author: Marnie Smith
work: Uniform semiclassical nonlinear Hartree phase mixing and weighted scattering for small perturbations
difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `densityofoperator` at source lines 500-506: for a kernel Q in H^0_{M,M} with M = ceil((d+1)/2), the Fourier transform of the density rho_Q(x) = Q(x,x) equals the partial Fourier transform of the kernel, in the two equivalent forms displayed. The proof (source lines 507-528) has to do two things that are independent: first the identity for Schwartz kernels, by Fourier inversion, Fubini and the substitution k' = k - p (lines 508-513), and then the extension to the weighted Sobolev space, which is not automatic because both sides must be shown to be continuous functionals, handled by a Cauchy-Schwarz and Sobolev-embedding estimate for sup_k of the p-integral (lines 515-525) in which the position and momentum multiplications are traded against the weight. Only after that does the density argument apply, and it is the retained earlier lemma that identifies the left-hand side with the Wigner transform at eta = 0 (line 527).
